analysis: Examined docs-only units. docs/developer/test.md head 2731-3434 is unchanged surrounding text in this batch; the actual change (head 2115-2131) adds a test description for the Model Requant Upload workflow (secret-free preflight, prod environment job, master-only ref guard, hash-pinned tools, upload holding only the chosen key set). docs/operations/model-revisions.md head 3 and 171-296 add a runbook for .github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml: CI rebuilds a re-quantized revision via scripts/models/requant.py, compares byte-for-byte to a locally qualified manifest, conditionally reserves (immutable upload rule) and uploads with R2 credentials; it never registers or promotes (Register Model remains a separate approval). The doc candidly notes residual risks: the prod environment's branch policy allows v* branches/tags and the ref guard only runs in the workflow copy executed (a writer pushing a v* branch with a modified workflow could reach PROD_R2_* after approval); repository R2_* secrets are readable by any workflow a writer pushes; objects are public at models.darkbloom.ai on landing but unselected until registered. These are CI/supply-chain concerns relating to A-004 (model weights) and the publication pipeline, which is largely outside this provider threat model's canonical entries; the workflow YAML, requant.py and tests are not in this batch, so their enforcement (input validation before secrets, manifest role checks, ref guard, secret scoping) cannot be verified here. No provider runtime behavior changes; provider-side weight-hash verification (T-012/T-027) is unaffected. Integration should check the workflow source in other batches for: secrets exposed to preflight, ref-guard bypass via v* branches, injection of dispatch inputs (manifest_json, URLs) into shell, and whether the threat model should record the CI model-upload credential boundary as new surface.
